card.name: Subject just before 'should' instructions
card.fires_on: The last word of a sentence subject (a drug, product, patient or noun like information or hours) right before an expected 'should' or 'is' instruction in label text.

modes.label: Drug or product as subject
modes.description: A drug name or product noun that is about to take 'should be discontinued' or 'should not be taken'.
modes.example: treatment with benazepril hydrochloride<< tablets>> should be discontinued and appropriate therapy instituted immediately

modes.label: Patient or condition before advice
modes.description: Patients or a symptom duration that leads into 'should seek medical attention'.
modes.example: Patients who have an erection lasting greater than 4<< hours>>, whether painful or not, should seek

modes.label: Dose statement subject
modes.description: The drug noun or verb right before a stated dose.
modes.example: The dosage of saxagliptin tablets<< is>> 2.5 mg orally once daily

card.writes: It suppresses Chinese words for advice such as 'best not to' and 'please', so it seems to push the model toward an English 'should' or 'will' next.
card.plain: It fires on the subject of a sentence just before the label says what should or should not be done.
